description: Declare a third-party kit — a kit of game logic compiled alone into one .wasm (a kit module), not one of GripForge's — in a local game, ISOLATED by default (a memory of its own) or, with trust "common", in the memory of the game (not isolated: only a kit the maker trusts). Reads one build of gripforge_third_party_kit_build (kit: its output folder; or wasm + manifest, file or http(s) URL), checks it (the binary against the manifest; against the core and the kits of the game's kit modules when the game has them; the kits it requires against the game), then writes: project.thirdPartyKits (source, sha256, manifest), its entry in project.installed (config), its place at the end of lock.order, and lock.thirdParty (version and sha256 frozen). A module given as a file is copied beside the game (third-party-kits/). A third-party module is loaded only when the game declares it; the page then plays the kit modules by itself. Use GripForge's kits first (gripforge_gamekit_search): a third-party kit is for a rule no kit has. check=true writes nothing. Calling it again with a new build replaces the kit. Guide: gripforge_docs { topic: "kit-third-party" }.

config.description: Config of the kit in the game (what kx.config() returns). Kept from the previous declaration when omitted.

game.description: Absolute path of the game: its game.json ({ "project": …, "lock": … }), or the folder that holds it (an exported web game).

kit.description: Absolute path of the output folder of gripforge_third_party_kit_build (it holds build.json): the build of the trust asked is taken from it. Use this, or wasm + manifest.

manifest.description: The .kit.json written beside the module by the build: absolute path, or an http(s) URL.

modules.description: Absolute path of a folder of kit modules (kit-modules.json) to check against and to install the module in. Default: <game folder>/runtime-rust/kit-modules, else <game folder>/kit-modules, when present.

trust.description: How far the game trusts this kit. "isolated" (default): the kit keeps a memory of its own and cannot read or corrupt the game — use it for any kit you did not write. "common": the kit is placed in the memory of the core and of the other kits, as a GripForge kit is — faster, and NOT isolated: only for a kit the maker of the game trusts. The build declared must be the one of that mode.

wasm.description: The kit module: absolute path of the .wasm, or an http(s) URL (with manifest; or give kit instead).

name: gripforge_third_party_kit_add
title: Declare a third-party kit in a game
